primary_crosschecks.verified: Primary intervention tables support the clean Qwen3 bidirectional refusal-direction reversal; other tested model families are partial/non-clean and bound the scope.

Primary 3x3 adaptive benchmark and replay data support heterogeneous/non-universal transfer and pooled-attacker coverage gains. Appendix provenance notes mean some raw directional replay rates include proxy/decoy wins; do not overread those cells.
Primary controlled reasoning-prefill intervention separates ACT from trajectory-dependent BCT robustness in the tested models.
Matched BASE/REFLEXION materials-discovery evidence supports episodic-memory gain and documents verbal-constraint non-compliance; the proposed enforceable actuator is not experimentally tested.

Primary sequential-evalue theory permits query-path boosting under the capped conditional expectation condition; inverse McNemar sampling supplies the fixed-discordant binomial null. Comparator arithmetic exactly reproduced the worker's stated r=20,q=.75,m=20 calibration.

General boosting maps are permitted by the cited method. Comparator arithmetic exactly reproduced floor c and expected log penalties for the stated finite-support null; utility remains worker-simulation evidence.
The cited method anchors the e-value setting; the late-signal collapse claim is a worker-local scoped log-product power derivation, not a theorem quoted from the source.
Primary e-detector/composite-e-process theory supports weighted e-process PFA constructions; the sparse frozen-anchor architecture and finite-memory power design are worker-local adaptations.
Standard ARL e-detector theory aggregates genuinely delayed e-processes. The worker's explicit preloaded-prefix counterexample is a scoped negative derivation against naive transfer.

deterministic_recomputation.interpretation: Independent arithmetic recomputation within this comparator matched the worker-local exact finite-support calculations; this is not independent empirical replication.

assessments.tested_scope: ACT versus base activation-direction interventions on the paper's held-out jailbreaks and tested model-specific steering strengths; strongest clean reversal on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-1.7B.
assessments.rationale: The primary study directly subtracts the learned refusal direction from ACT and applies the opposite intervention to base models. Qwen3-8B ACT refusal falls from about 96% unsteered to 1.2% [0.2,6.6] at alpha=10 while base+direction reaches 100%; Qwen3-1.7B shows the same bidirectional flip. This is unusually direct causal evidence for a white-box single-point-of-failure in the tested ACT representations.
limits: Requires internal activation access and a direction derived from ACT-vs-base activations.
Other tested families show partial or non-clean reversals; do not generalize to every model or activation-based defense.
No black-box/API attack implication and no independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Adaptive Adversaries 15-round three-attacker by three-defender benchmark and its discovered-win replay transfer analysis.
assessments.rationale: The study provides a large 3x3 interaction matrix, 78 pairwise-distinct genuine winning turns, pooled-attacker coverage gains of about 1.4-2.2x, and no universal replay winner among 46 unique replay attacks. This strongly supports defender-specific failure surfaces and the inadequacy of one-source replay corpora. Raw directional transfer percentages are less clean because the appendix notes that replay data predated final hardening and some cells include proxy/decoy wins.
limits: Use the robust non-universal/heterogeneous-transfer conclusion rather than treating every directional percentage as a clean final-defense success rate.
Attacker axis is frontier model identity/online interaction, not multiple independently seeded trained best responses per frozen defender.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: ACT versus BCT on held-out jailbreaks with compliant base-model chain-of-thought prefills and post-thinking continuation under the paper's tested models.
assessments.rationale: The same primary study intervenes on the reasoning trajectory rather than only scoring normal rollouts. ACT refuses at least 98% of prefilled jailbreaks on every tested model while BCT loses robustness on most; on Qwen3-8B ACT continues a malicious-looking open-ended trace for about 342 tokens on average before self-correcting and refuses 95%, and it refuses all 82 cases when both compliant reasoning and the first answer sentence are prefilled. This is direct evidence that ordinary rollout safety can hide trajectory dependence.
limits: The trace is injected from the corresponding undefended base model with white-box/prefill control.
The contrast is ACT versus the tested BCT construction, not all output-supervised safety training.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: MADE closed-loop materials discovery, 30 chemical systems over 8 episodes for two Qwen model scales, comparing BASE and episodic REFLEXION with otherwise matched agent/tools/prompts.
assessments.rationale: The cited study gives a matched memory benefit: stable discoveries rise 9.82->14.43 and 14.82->21.28 with p<1e-4, while fitted cross-episode slopes improve. It simultaneously documents reduced breadth and cases where the actor ignores verbal diversification/cap/exclusion instructions. That supports the need for stronger control than advisory reflection, but the worker's proposed machine-enforceable actuator is a new mechanism hypothesis and was not tested.
limits: Breadth collapse was observed in the tested benchmark; predicted sparse-space failure was not directly tested.
No matched experiment compares verbal reflection with an enforceable constraint actuator.
Workshop evidence, two model scales, one materials-discovery environment.

assessments.tested_scope: Fixed-discordant paired binary audit with r=20, sign bet q=0.75, SeqE-Guard cap m=20, plus stated negative-binomial task-cost model; candidate-level rather than arbitrary per-task scalar boosting.
assessments.rationale: Inverse McNemar sampling supplies an exact Binomial(r,1/2) null for discordant signs, and Fischer-Ramdas permits query-path boosting of sequential e-values under the required conditional expectation bound. Independent algebraic recomputation in this comparator exactly matched the worker's raw truncated null mean 0.7033378188 and maximal scalar boost b=1.5309913291. The construction is therefore mechanically coherent, but its agent-level utility remains worker-local.
limits: Random total paired-task cost can be high when discordance is rare.
This recomputation verifies arithmetic, not an independent empirical replication of a deployed agent.
Validity still depends on predictable/frozen audit design and the cited query-path conditions.

assessments.tested_scope: General query-path boost g_c(E)=max(E,c) for the fixed-discordant r=20, q=0.75 candidate-level null with m=20, and the worker's deterministic/Markov stress-test regimes.
assessments.rationale: Fischer-Ramdas explicitly allows general boosting maps, not only scalar multiplication. Comparator recomputation matched the worker's maximal floor c=0.4511525134 and expected null log penalty -0.6772343230 versus -3.0261899991 raw. This verifies the exact finite-support calibration for the stated query path. The claimed routing benefit is still simulation-local and the worker correctly finds that the boost fades as the cap grows.
limits: Query-path-specific boosting need not improve other paths.
The transform does not cure the structural long-null delayed-signal collapse.
No real-agent matched experiment or independent empirical replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Fixed strict-commit query path and iid/nondegenerate null candidate e-values with positive lower-tail mass and finite expected absolute log of min(Z,1); adaptive/dependent streams require extra assumptions.
assessments.rationale: The log-product argument is mathematically straightforward: every off-query factor below one multiplies future wealth downward, and under the stated iid conditions the average log penalty converges to a negative constant, so the evidence threshold grows exponentially. The worker's stress tests are consistent with this late-signal power pathology. This is a power result, not a Type-I-validity failure.
limits: The asymptotic result is scoped to the stated fixed/iid conditions.
Adaptive/dependent candidate streams need conditional-drift or ergodic analysis.
No external empirical replication of the exact agent-facing product controller.

assessments.tested_scope: Deterministic sparse candidate starts/expiries and globally summable start prior; proper predictable likelihoods with absolute continuity; outer infimum after forming each null-specific weighted killed wealth. Gaussian power experiments are local engineering evidence only.
assessments.rationale: The PFA argument is well aligned with primary e-detector/composite-e-process theory: killed null-specific likelihood-ratio wealths are supermartingales, a weighted sum with total initial mass <=1 remains valid, and the outer infimum is pointwise dominated by each null-specific process. The finite-memory tail collapse and telescoping start prior are concrete engineering refinements. Worker Monte Carlo gives a useful power/memory check but is not the validity proof.
limits: Current theorem is PFA mode, not the standard finite-ARL e-detector guarantee.
Data-adaptive start/expiry selection and unknown-variance transfer need separate validity arguments.
No independent numerical replication of the worker Monte Carlo.

assessments.tested_scope: Standard finite-ARL e-detector sum semantics versus frozen-anchor full-prefix candidate wealth inserted only at its nominal split; the worker gives an explicit stopping-time counterexample.
assessments.rationale: Primary e-detector theory obtains ARL control from genuinely delayed/start-time e-process aggregation. The worker's counterexample shows why a full-prefix martingale cannot simply be 'added at split time' without importing pre-split wealth: the stopping-time e-detector inequality is violated in the constructed case. This is strong negative structural evidence for the naive transfer and justifies separating PFA and ARL modes.
limits: Counterexample rejects the naive construction, not every possible ARL-valid frozen-anchor architecture.
A different capital-accounting or normalized delayed process might recover ARL semantics at a cost to information.
No deployed-system replication is relevant to this theorem-bound result.

material_scope_corrections: FE-107 supports heterogeneous/non-universal cross-defender transfer, but raw directional replay percentages must retain the source's proxy/decoy provenance caveat.
sci-agent-clean-g1-042 has matched evidence for episodic reflection memory and observed verbal-control failure; the machine-enforceable actuator extension remains untested.
eval-g1-query-path-floor-boost-v1 reduces early off-query penalty in the stated calibration but does not solve long-null delayed-signal collapse.
cf-g1-r67 finite-memory frozen-anchor construction is presently PFA-mode; standard finite-ARL e-detector semantics do not transfer by simply adding full-prefix wealth at the split.
